title.narrative: Strengthen Infonavit sustainable urbanization and adequate housing actions within the framework of the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda

description.narrative:
This proposal seeks to provide technical assistance to the Institute of the National Fund for Workers' Housing (Infonavit) in the development of a set of actionable strategies on urban planning, generation of spatial indicators at a city scale, and integration of value chains in the housing construction sector that allow the Institute's housing finance initiatives to integrate into a more sustainable urbanization landscape and help ensure the right to adequate housing for all of Infonavit's borrowers and beneficiaries.
This will enable the Institute to support the fulfilment of the goals and objectives of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, using an approach in which adequate housing is a central element for sustainable urbanization and prosperity. The proposal has three main strategic lines:
Strategic line 1. Urban planning at the municipal level Objective To develop a collaborative strategy for the elaboration, strengthening and improvement of municipal urban development plans and programmes in Mexico, according to international standards, and to promote their successful implementation at the local scale, based on a replicable methodology that facilitates the future development and upgrading of municipal planning instruments.
Strategic line 2. Generation of evidence for decision making Objective Generate strategic information at the urban scale to establish a baseline for progress in meeting the SDGs in 25 strategic municipalities in the country and, from this, define a monitoring scheme that supports decision-making on housing, urban planning, land, and financing of projects with SDG impact for all actors in the sector. This is in line with the guidelines of the SDG Cities flagship programme promoted globally by UN-Habitat.
Strategic line 3. Strengthening value chains in the housing sector Objective Propose a set of policy actions to consolidate the integration of national value chains associated with the housing construction sector, particularly those related to housing financing activities promoted by Infonavit, as well as other infrastructure, land, public spaces, or mobility activities promoted by the public sector.
Approach Based on its experience of more than 40 years, both normative and operational, as well as in specialized research, databases, international best practices in urban and territorial development, UN-Habitat proposes an intervention strategy that includes following approaches:
- Integrated territorial development: UN-Habitat will support Infonavit´s efforts to develop urban planning instruments, planning frameworks and housing actions that boost the productivity of cities and regions through an integrated territorial development approach.
- Human-rights: All the work carried out by UN-Habitat will be underpinned by a human-rights-based approach, which ensures that those furthest behind are targeted first.
- Multilevel governance: UN-Habitat will promote multilevel governance approaches so that national governments empower local governments to take climate action through improved frameworks with strong local-national collaboration.
- Adaptation to the context: each city is subjected to specific sets of conditions. UN-Habitat will work based on a differentiated and participative approach to best support cities in implementing the New Urban Agenda and achieving the urban dimensions of the Sustainable Development Goals. This approach will consider the typology developed in the context of UN-Habitat´s new Strategic Plan.
- Scale-up impact: a catalytic approach in which UN-Habitat leverages its knowledge, technical cooperation, convening capacity, partnerships and advocacy (“Think, do, partner, share”) for scaled-up impact to achieve sustainable urban development.
Expected accomplishments - Expected accomplishment 1: Infonavit has 10 local urban planning instruments for strategic municipalities and promotes technical tools to create and update these instruments in Mexican municipalities. - Expected accomplishment 2: Infonavit has and promotes among Mexican cities a monitoring scheme to make urban policy decisions based on evidence, and to measure progress in the implementation of the SDGs and the NAU at the local level. - Expected accomplishment 3: Infonavit has and promotes among stakeholders a strategy to strengthen integrated value chains, based on investments in housing and infrastructure joined into its urban context.
